conviction_note: The stock trades on the first FY27 net income guide. Deere opened FY26 about 25% below consensus ($4.0B against $5.31B) and fell 5.7%. FY27 consensus is quoted at +22% to +28% EPS growth (about $22.3-23, roughly $6B net income), which is hard to square with management's 'measured recovery, not a sharp rebound', a net tariff step-up from about $750M to about $1B and the $382M refund rolling off. That is a sizeable guide risk, but the FY27 bar has no dated dollar source, so the finding is capped. Partly offsetting are counterparty data that landed after Deere last spoke: AEM October 4WD tractors up 7.7%, AGCO North America early orders up high teens, Titan raising its ag assumption on Nov 24, and Deere recalling every laid-off worker. Puts are already bid (+11.9 vol points of skew) and the stock is down 5.1% in 5 days with short interest low. p_up 47 on a 6.0% scale gives -0.36. The findings sum to +0.7 because most small counterparty items lean positive while the one large item, the guide, leans negative and is capped.
bar: Q4 FY26 EPS consensus $4.07 (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-18, https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/DE/23254; whisper $4.30) and $4.06 / net income $1,082M (Hudson Labs, 2026-10-26, https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/deere-q4-2026-earnings-preview-de-revenue-guidance-key-risks). Revenue about $10.30-10.35B. Company FY26 net income guide is $4.75-5.00B against $3.808B year to date, so the implied Q4 is $0.94-1.19B and consensus sits in the upper half (8-K 2026-08-20, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm). The FY27 bar, which the stock trades on, is NOT sourced in dollars to a current, dated document: Zacks quotes FY27 EPS growth of 22.4% (https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2979235/can-construction-and-forestry-fuel-deeres-long-term-growth, date unverified) or 27.9%, and Barchart quotes $22.40 (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/37082841/what-to-expect-from-deere-company-s-next-quarterly-earnings-report, undated). Guidance findings are capped small for that reason.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 5.2M shares, roughly 1.9% of shares outstanding, with about 4.2 days to cover, as of the 2026-11-05 settlement (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/DE). Massive.com gives 5.75M short and 4.3 days for 2026-09-30. Not crowded. The baseline shows 25-delta skew of +11.94 vol points (downside paid), a put/call OI ratio of 0.80, an event-implied move of 4.78% (straddle 5.35%), a 5-day run-up of -5.12%, a 20-day of -3.68%, and the stock 13.2% below its 52-week high. Earnings Whispers bullish sentiment is 22.8% (https://finviz.com/news/424950/deeres-fourth-quarter-must-prove-fiscal-2026-was-the-bottom-of-the-farm-cycle). The skew agrees with the negative guide finding, so that finding is partly priced. The broad tape was risk-off in mid-November (S&P -1.9% on 11-16 and -1% on 11-17, https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3031068/stock-market-news-for-nov-17-2026).

findings.finding: The FY27 first guide is at risk of landing below consensus. Deere's own Aug-20 framing was a 'measured recovery rather than a sharp rebound in 2027'. The CFO put net tariffs at about $1B in FY27 against about $750M in FY26, and FY26 carried $382M of non-recurring IEEPA refunds (pre-tax). FY26 net income therefore runs about $4.6B ex-refunds against a $4.75-5.0B guide. FY27 consensus quotes +22% to +28% EPS growth (about $22.3-23 EPS, roughly $6.0-6.3B net income), which needs about +30% underlying. Last year the first guide came about 25% below consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025: initial FY26 guide of about $4.0B net income against $5.31B consensus, stock -5.67% despite a Q4 beat (https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/investing/investor-outlook/2025/11/26/investor-outlook-deere-outlook-flags-2026-as-low-point-for-large-ag-cycle/). Aug 2026: guide low end raised, +6.94%. May 2026: -5.19%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: skew +11.9 and the stock -5% in 5 days lean the same way. What may not be priced is the size of the gap. If the Street had fully cut FY27 toward a measured-recovery path, the previews would quote a FY27 number near FY26 plus 10%, not +22-28%. The Nov-18 Earnings Whispers preview still frames the report as a test of a 'growth case'.
findings.independence: Supply Chain Dive, 2026-08-25, CFO on the tariff step-up (https://supplychaindive.com/news/deere-expects-step-up-in-tariff-costs-in-2027/828624). The FY27 consensus figures come from Zacks/Barchart pages whose dates are unverified, so the bar is capped. Shares the Q3 transcript with the Q4 finding.

findings.finding: Q4 FY26 should land at or modestly above the $4.07 consensus. Consensus sits in the upper half of the guide-implied Q4 net income of $0.94-1.19B. Deere beat Q3 by about $0.31 (+6.5%) and raised the guide low end, and the whisper is $4.30. Against that, management said it 'pulled ahead some demand' from Q4 into Q3, Q4 PPA/C&F sales are flat with Q3, Q4 PPA/SAT margins are lower on seasonal R&D/SA&G, and no Q4 refunds are assumed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025: Q4 beat, stock -5.67% on the guide. Aug 2026: beat, +6.94% with the guide raised. The quarter on its own has not decided the move; the guide has.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the whisper is $0.23 above consensus, so a modest beat is expected. Inside the company's guided range.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-18 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/DE/23254). The Q3 call transcript gives the Q4 bridge (same document as the guidance finding).

findings.finding: Titan Machinery, the largest CNH (Case IH) dealer, reported on 2026-11-24, after Deere last spoke. It raised its FY27 ag revenue assumption to -10% to -15% from -15% to -20%, on year-to-date and Q4 expectations. Ag same-store sales were -13.1% in the Aug-Oct quarter, and the CEO said the late-summer commodity price rise 'did not last'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured DE reaction to Titan prints. Titan reports the day before or near Deere most years.
findings.why_not_priced: Out on 11-24 and partly in today's DE close of $616.02. It is a CNH-brand dealer, so the read to Deere's North American retail is indirect. If the market had read it as a demand floor, DE would not have closed at a 5-day low.
findings.independence: AEM October data (https://www.rfdtv.com/four-wheel-drive-tractor-sales-rise-despite-broader-equipment-weakness) also points to stabilising North American retail. Proxy: not a Deere number.

findings.finding: AEM October 2026 US retail: 4WD tractors 337 units, +7.7% y/y; total tractors -0.5%; combines -9.6%. Year to date tractors are -11.6% and 4WD -19%, so October, the first month of Deere's FY27, was the best y/y print for large tractors in the year. September tractors were -16.4%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured for DE on AEM releases.
findings.source_date: 2026-11 (October 2026 AEM data; the article page carries no explicit date, and the 2026 year is confirmed by the YTD comparison to 2025)
findings.why_not_priced: Public industry series, so partly priced. Combines are still -9.6%. If the market had read October as a turn, the stock would not be down 5% into the print with puts bid.

findings.finding: Deere release, 2026-10-30: it will hire 400+ workers at Illinois, Iowa and Kansas factories and recall 275+ to Waterloo (large tractors). Every employee still laid off in Waterloo, the Quad Cities, Ottumwa and Dubuque has been called back; about 125 remain laid off in Des Moines. That is a production step-up into FY27, which helps absorption. A spokesperson tied it to building dealer inventory before planting/harvest and to continuity through UAW talks; the contract expires 2027-10-31 after talks collapsed in August 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured. Production versus retail has been central to Deere guide reactions (Nov 2025 underproduction, -5.7%).
findings.why_not_priced: Reported in local and trade press, not in the earnings previews, which do not mention FY27 production levels. If priced as a ramp, the FY27 previews would talk of production up and better decrementals. Part of it is a pre-strike build, which is lower quality, so it is sized net.
findings.independence: AgWeb report of the same release (https://www.agweb.com/news/john-deere-recalls-275-staff-opens-400-factory-jobs). Same underlying release, counted once.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-04 Deere announced it will close the Ottumwa (windrowers, balers) and Clarion/Hagie (sprayers) Iowa plants by 2028-2029 and move sugar cane harvesters to Brazil. Deere said it is 'operating far below normal production volumes'. No charge was quantified, and the 8-K of 11-02 covers only board items. Restructuring costs could appear in the Q4 results or the FY27 guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Small, multi-year, and the charge is unquantified. The market typically looks through footprint moves.

findings.finding: Peers who reported after Deere's August call lean toward a North American recovery in 2027. AGCO (Oct 29): North American Q3 sales +35% at constant currency, North American early orders up high teens, management sees 'some recovery coming in 2027' and called North America 'probably the most positive market globally'. CNH (Nov 9): North American industry >140HP tractors -5%, combines -13% in Q3, and it is positioning for a 'potential market upturn in North America in 2027'; Q3 ag EBIT was helped by IEEPA refunds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured for DE on peer prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Public peer data, weeks old, so largely priced. AGCO's lowered EPS and CNH's weak combines keep it mixed.
findings.independence: CNH Q3 release (https://finviz.com/news/418826/cnh-industrial-nv-reports-third-quarter-2026-results). Peers, not Deere's numbers.

findings.finding: Crop prices have fallen since the Aug-20 call. Management cited corn futures 'about $5.05' as a good signal; on 2026-11-18 Dec corn closed $4.355 and Dec-2027 corn $4.7475. Wheat Dec is $5.70. Soybeans are firm at $12.17 for January. The corn half of the farm-income support management leaned on has faded.
findings.why_not_priced: Futures prices are public, so mostly priced. The open question is whether Deere's FY27 large-ag industry guide assumes the August price deck.
findings.independence: Titan CEO: the late-summer commodity rise 'did not last' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001409171/000162828026075606/afy27q3ex991earningsrelease.htm). Macro-to-company transmission, proxy.

findings.finding: Purdue/CME Ag Economy Barometer for October 2026 (released Nov 3): the Farm Capital Investment Index jumped from 39 to 55 and the headline from 123 to 126, though only 20% say now is a good time to buy machinery. Improvement was tied to government payments.
findings.why_not_priced: Public survey, partly priced. Sentiment is a soft proxy.
findings.independence: Beef Magazine on the same survey (https://www.beefmagazine.com/farm-business-management/producer-optimism-grows-in-october-as-current-conditions-improve). One survey, counted once.

findings.finding: Possible unguided Q4 IEEPA refund. Deere assumed no refunds in Q4 (Aug-Oct) after $110M in Q3 that arrived 'slightly above expectations, due to the timing of Phase 2'. CBP had certified about $122B by mid-September and opened CAPE Phase 3 on Oct 6. CNH and Caterpillar recognised refunds in their September quarters.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: May 2026: the $272M refund-inflated beat went with -5.19%, so refunds have not been paid for by this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: The previews explicitly say no Q4 refunds, so any refund is outside consensus. It is below-the-line quality and non-recurring with no path to the FY27 guide, so it is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: Q3 transcript: Deere's statement that Q3 refund timing came 'slightly above expectations' (https://s22.q4cdn.com/253594569/files/doc_financials/2026/q3/DE-3Q26-Earnings-Call-Transcript.pdf).

findings.finding: Positioning is already defensive into the print. Skew is +11.94 vol points with puts bid, the stock is -5.12% over 5 days and 13% off its 52-week high, short interest is low (about 1.9% of shares, 4.2 days), and bullish sentiment is 22.8%. A guide merely in line with a trimmed Street can relieve the hedges.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026 +11.58% after a pre-print slide on farm-demand worries (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/de-stock-heads-for-another-day-in-red-traders-brace-for-q1-earnings/cZRj8fnR4w0).
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. It is sized small because it runs against the skew, and the option market may simply be right about the guide.
findings.independence: Sealed baseline skew and run-up. Earnings Whispers sentiment (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/DE/23254).

findings.finding: The construction read from Caterpillar is strong for Deere C&F, about a third of equipment sales. CAT Q3 2026 sales +17% and Construction Industries profit +33%, on North American end-user demand, data centers and infrastructure. Deere already said its C&F backlog extends 'well into fiscal 2027' and it underproduced C&F retail in FY26, a setup for FY27 shipments above retail. CAT shares fell about 4% on a trimmed outlook and dealer-inventory effects.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: Deere's C&F strength is known, and the previews name the backlog. What remains is upside to the FY27 C&F guide from the underproduction refill.
findings.independence: Deere Q3 transcript, C&F backlog and underproduction (https://s22.q4cdn.com/253594569/files/doc_financials/2026/q3/DE-3Q26-Earnings-Call-Transcript.pdf).

outside_window.finding: The UAW contract expires 2027-10-31 after talks collapsed in August 2026. A strike risk for FY28 production and a pre-build in FY27.
Purdue November barometer, due 2026-12-01, after the window.

baseline_tension: The one large finding, FY27 guide risk, agrees with the +11.9 put skew and the -5% run-in, so it is partly priced. The small counterparty findings lean positive against the skew. Net, I sit slightly below 50 and do not fight the options market.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the FY27 consensus has no dated dollar source, so the guidance finding is capped from -1.5 to -1.0 and p_up moves from 46 to 47.
Two findings on one fact: the tariff step-up (-0.3) is merged into the guide finding and listed in rejected_candidates as a duplicate.
Lesson 1 (a fact is not a reaction): the Q4 beat goes from +0.3 to +0.2, because this stock has traded the guide and not the quarter (Nov 2025 beat, -5.7%).
Lesson 2 (one-offs as one-offs): the possible Q4 IEEPA refund goes from +0.2 to +0.1.
Lesson 3 (the caveat reaches the number): the hiring/recall finding carries its own UAW pre-build caveat and goes from +0.5 to +0.3.
Lesson 5 (proxies smaller): the crop-price macro transmission goes from -0.5 to -0.3.
Lesson 7 (positioning against the skew): the positioning-relief finding goes from +0.3 to +0.2.
abs_move_pct is raised from 5.8 to 6.0 because a first guide is likely and the hunters have understated moves (Lesson 8 / core).
